title: MisspecificationProbe: A Lightweight Toolkit for Detecting Reward Model Misspecification

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Direct chain: detecting reward model misspecification before RLHF training prevents the propagation of proxy-learning into the final model. Addresses a well-documented failure mode with concrete practical value.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building controlled probe pairs (length-controlled, apology-injected, formatting-varied) and running them through reward models is moderately complex. Requires loading reward models and creating well-matched stimulus pairs, which needs some ML familiarity beyond beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three probe types with normalized sensitivity scores is a reasonable scope, but creating genuinely controlled pairs where only one variable changes requires careful dataset construction. Achievable in 30 hours if limited to 2-3 reward models.
